si_thresholds: persistent wheeze or dyspnea after initial treatment
is_requirements: repeated short-acting bronchodilator and ipratropium dosing
two_midnight_expectation: Often under two midnights when lung function and oxygenation improve after initial treatment; longer when acute-care bronchodilator need and obstruction persist.
denial_downgrade_triggers: subjective symptoms only without objective reassessment
overturn_support_factors: persistent objective obstruction after initial therapy
observation_features: safe home action plan in place

gap_questions.question: What was the one-hour reassessment response?
Is the patient still desaturating or requiring repeated bronchodilators?
Can the home action plan be executed safely?

documentation_phrases.phrase: I expect medically necessary hospital care to span at least two midnights because the patient requires hospital-only services that cannot be safely delivered at a lower level of care.
Lower-level care is not safe because the patient requires the hospital-only services documented above with ongoing reassessment.

citations.locator: UR plan; medical necessity of admissions and continued stays
acute exacerbation severity, monitoring, hospitalization decision
